exposure: Maternal serum 25-hydroxy-vitamin D [25(OH)D] status in early and mid-pregnancy
Consistently deficient (DD) 25(OH)D status (<10ng/mL) across both trimesters
Initially deficient then sufficient (DS) 25(OH)D status (normalized in second trimester)
Consistently sufficient (SS) 25(OH)D status (>=20ng/mL) across both trimesters
cohort: The study reviewed clinical records of 5,169 singleton pregnant women who received two serum 25(OH)D tests in the first and second trimesters between 2016 and 2022.
finding: Maternal vitamin D deficiency present in both early and mid-pregnancy (DD group) was associated with significantly elevated risks of preterm birth before 34 weeks, necrotizing enterocolitis, and developmental delay, and these risks were not diminished even when vitamin D deficiency was corrected in the second trimester (DS group).
